newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral says no compromise on Kashmir - paper.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral says no compromise on Kashmir - paper.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral has indicated that India would not compromise with Pakistan over the divided region of Kashmir in bilateral negotiations due to be held on Monday.

In an interview with the Economic Times published on Monday Gujral said: "It must be understood that there are certain irreducible interests in every country and the secular unity and territorial integrity of India is one such."
"There can be no compromise on these issues."

Gujral was apparently referring to the Himalayan region of Kashmir, over which India and Pakistan have fought two wars since 1947. India controls two-thirds of Kashmir and Pakistan the rest, but each claims the entire territory.

Gujral was speaking to the newspaper before he left for a regional summit in the Maldives. He is due to meet Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif on Monday on the sidelines of the conference, the first time the leaders of the two arch-rivals were to hold talks in four years.

Diplomats have cautioned against expectations of a quick breakthrough in the talks. The two nations launched bilateral talks in March after a three-year hiatus marked by tension over Kashmir, where officials say more than 20,000 people have died in a separatist insurgency.
New Delhi says Kashmir is an integral part of India.

Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan on Sunday indicated that while Pakistan continued to insist Kashmir should be on the agenda in bilateral talks, it was willing to allow progress in less contentious areas -- a stand welcomed by India.
"It has been my perception that upon India devolves the main responsibility for stepping up cooperation in the region," Gujral told the daily.
"I believe that it is in keeping with our tradition to offer unstinted cooperation without any short-term calculation of costs and benefits."
